stem: Water flows into a reservoir at a rate of F(t) thousand liters per hour, where t is the number of hours after midnight. At t = 6, F(6) = 4.2 and F′(6) = −0.5. Which statement is correct at t = 6?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The volume of water is decreasing at 0.5 thousand liters per hour.
choices.rationale: This treats F′(6) as the rate of change of the volume, but F itself is the volume's rate of change, so F′ is the rate at which the inflow rate is changing.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The volume of water is decreasing, because F′(6) is negative.
choices.rationale: The sign of F′ shows whether the inflow rate is rising or falling, not whether the volume is rising; the volume rises because F(6) = 4.2 is positive.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The volume of water is increasing at 4.2 thousand liters per hour, and that rate of increase is decreasing at 0.5 thousand liters per hour per hour.
choices.rationale: Correct: The volume V satisfies V′(t) = F(t), so V′(6) = 4.2 > 0 and the volume is increasing. Also V″(6) = F′(6) = −0.5, so the rate of increase is falling by 0.5 thousand liters per hour each hour.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The inflow rate will be exactly 3.7 thousand liters per hour at t = 7.
choices.rationale: F′(6) is an instantaneous rate at t = 6, so multiplying it by one hour only approximates the change in F and does not give an exact value.

title: interpret the derivative of a rate function in context, with units and sign, without confusing the rate with its own rat (variant 1)
stem: Water leaves a lake through a dam at a rate of D(t) million gallons per day, where t is measured in days. At t = 10, D(10) = 3.0 and D′(10) = 0.4. Which statement is correct at t = 10?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The volume of the lake is increasing at 0.4 million gallons per day.
choices.rationale: This reads D′(10) as the rate of change of the volume; the volume's rate of change is −D(10), while D′ describes how the outflow rate itself is changing.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The volume of the lake is increasing at 3.0 million gallons per day, because D′(10) is positive.
choices.rationale: A positive D′ means the outflow rate is rising, not that the lake is filling; water is leaving, so the volume decreases whenever D(10) is positive.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The volume of the lake is decreasing at 3.0 million gallons per day, and the outflow rate is increasing at 0.4 million gallons per day per day.
choices.rationale: Correct: Volume V satisfies V′(t) = −D(t), so V′(10) = −3.0 and the volume is decreasing at 3.0 million gallons per day. D′(10) = 0.4 > 0 means the outflow rate is rising by 0.4 million gallons per day each day.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The outflow rate will be exactly 3.4 million gallons per day at t = 11.
choices.rationale: D′(10) = 0.4 is an instantaneous rate at t = 10; adding it to D(10) for one full day is only an approximation, not an exact value.

title: interpret the derivative of a rate function in context, with units and sign, without confusing the rate with its own rat (variant 2)
stem: The rate at which customers enter a store is c(t) customers per minute, where t is the number of minutes after the store opens. At t = 20, c(20) = 6 and c′(20) = 0.3. Which statement is correct at t = 20?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The number of customers who have entered is increasing at 0.3 customers per minute.
choices.rationale: 0.3 is the value of c′(20), the rate at which the entry rate is changing; the number of customers who have entered changes at the entry rate c(20) = 6.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Customers are entering at 0.3 customers per minute at t = 20.
choices.rationale: The entry rate at t = 20 is c(20) = 6 customers per minute; c′(20) = 0.3 has units of customers per minute per minute and measures how that rate is changing.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The entry rate will be exactly 6.3 customers per minute at t = 21.
choices.rationale: The derivative is an instantaneous rate at t = 20, so using it over a full minute only approximates the new entry rate; it does not give an exact value.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The number of customers who have entered is increasing at 6 customers per minute, and that rate is increasing at 0.3 customers per minute per minute.
choices.rationale: Correct: The count N of customers who have entered satisfies N′(t) = c(t), so N′(20) = 6 customers per minute. c′(20) = 0.3 > 0, so the entry rate itself is rising at 0.3 customers per minute each minute.

title: interpret the derivative of a rate function in context, with units and sign, without confusing the rate with its own rat (variant 3)
stem: Oil is pumped out of a storage tank at a rate of p(t) hundred barrels per hour, where t is measured in hours. At t = 3, p(3) = 5.5 and p′(3) = −0.8. Which statement is correct at t = 3?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The volume of oil is increasing at 0.8 hundred barrels per hour, because the pumping rate is falling.
choices.rationale: A falling pumping rate means oil still leaves the tank, only more slowly; the volume keeps decreasing as long as p(3) is positive.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The volume of oil is decreasing at 5.5 hundred barrels per hour, and it is decreasing faster as time passes.
choices.rationale: P′(3) is negative, so the pumping rate is shrinking; the volume's rate of change −p(t) rises toward zero, which is a slowing decrease and not a faster one.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The pumping rate will be exactly 4.7 hundred barrels per hour at t = 4.
choices.rationale: P′(3) = −0.8 is an instantaneous rate at t = 3, so applying it over one full hour gives only an approximation of p(4), not an exact value.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The volume of oil is decreasing at 5.5 hundred barrels per hour, and it is decreasing more slowly as time passes.
choices.rationale: Correct: The volume V satisfies V′(t) = −p(t), so V′(3) = −5.5 (decreasing at 5.5). V″(3) = −p′(3) = 0.8 > 0, so V′ is rising toward zero and the decrease is slowing.

title: decide when a particle is speeding up by comparing the signs of velocity and acceleration, not either sign alone.
stem: A particle moves along the x-axis with velocity v(t) = t² − 5t + 4 for 0 ≤ t ≤ 6. On which time intervals is the particle speeding up?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: Correct: v = (t − 1)(t − 4) and a = 2t − 5. v and a are both negative on 1 < t < 2.5 and both positive on 4 < t < 6, so the particle speeds up exactly there.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: These are the intervals where v is positive; speeding up needs v and a to share a sign, and on 0 < t < 1 the velocity is positive while a = 2t − 5 is negative, so the particle slows down.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: This is where a is positive, but on 2.5 < t < 4 the velocity is negative while a is positive, so the particle is slowing down on that stretch.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: This is where v is negative, meaning the particle moves left, but moving left is not the same as speeding up; on 2.5 < t < 4 the acceleration is positive, so it slows.

title: distinguish total distance traveled from displacement and final position when velocity changes sign.
stem: A particle moves along a horizontal line with velocity v(t) = 3t² − 12t + 9 for 0 ≤ t ≤ 4. Its position at t = 0 is x(0) = 2. What is the total distance traveled by the particle from t = 0 to t = 4?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: Correct: v = 3(t − 1)(t − 3), and an antiderivative is t³ − 6t² + 9t, which equals 0 at t = 0, 4 at t = 1, 0 at t = 3 and 4 at t = 4. Distance = |4 − 0| + |0 − 4| + |4 − 0| = 12.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: This is the displacement x(4) − x(0); it lets the leftward motion on 1 < t < 3 cancel part of the rightward motion instead of adding to the distance.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: This is the final position x(4) = 2 + 4, which includes the starting position and is not a distance traveled.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: This counts only 0 ≤ t ≤ 3 and leaves out the final stretch 3 ≤ t ≤ 4, where the particle moves right again by 4 units.

title: distinguish total distance traveled from displacement and final position when velocity changes sign. (variant 1)
stem: A particle moves along a horizontal line with velocity v(t) = 6t² − 30t + 24 for 0 ≤ t ≤ 5. Its position at t = 0 is x(0) = 3. What is the total distance traveled by the particle from t = 0 to t = 5?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: This is the size of the displacement x(5) − x(0) = −5; the rightward and leftward motion partly cancel in displacement but both count toward distance.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: Correct: v = 6(t − 1)(t − 4), and an antiderivative is 2t³ − 15t² + 24t, which equals 0 at t = 0, 11 at t = 1, −16 at t = 4 and −5 at t = 5. Distance = 11 + 27 + 11 = 49.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: This adds only the two stretches where v is positive, 11 each, and omits the 27 units traveled while the particle moves left.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: This adds the first two stretches, 11 and 27, but leaves out the final stretch 4 ≤ t ≤ 5, where the particle moves right by another 11 units.

title: distinguish total distance traveled from displacement and final position when velocity changes sign. (variant 2)
stem: A particle moves along a horizontal line with velocity v(t) = cos t for 0 ≤ t ≤ 3π/2. Its position at t = 0 is x(0) = 5. What is the total distance traveled by the particle from t = 0 to t = 3π/2?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: This is the size of the displacement, sin(3π/2) − sin 0 = −1, in which the leftward and rightward motion cancel; distance adds them instead.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: This counts only the leftward motion on π/2 < t < 3π/2 and leaves out the 1 unit traveled right on 0 < t < π/2.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: This is the final position x(3π/2) = 5 − 1, which includes the starting position and is not a distance traveled.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: Correct: The integral of |cos t| splits at t = π/2: ∫ from 0 to π/2 of cos t dt = 1 and ∫ from π/2 to 3π/2 of |cos t| dt = 2. Total distance = 1 + 2 = 3.

title: distinguish total distance traveled from displacement and final position when velocity changes sign. (variant 3)
stem: A particle moves along a horizontal line with velocity v(t) = 4 − t² for 0 ≤ t ≤ 4. Its position at t = 0 is x(0) = 1. What is the total distance traveled by the particle from t = 0 to t = 4?

choices.label: A

choices.label: D

title: combine marginal revenue and marginal cost into a marginal profit and read the sign of the second derivative as the tren
stem: A company's revenue from selling x hundred units is R(x) = 50x − 0.5x² thousand dollars and its cost is C(x) = 20 + 12x + 0.1x² thousand dollars. Which statement is correct at x = 20?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Profit is increasing at 14 thousand dollars per hundred units, and that rate of increase is itself decreasing.
choices.rationale: Correct: P(x) = R(x) − C(x), so P′(x) = (50 − x) − (12 + 0.2x) = 38 − 1.2x and P′(20) = 14 > 0. P″(x) = −1.2 < 0, so the rate of profit increase is itself decreasing.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Profit is increasing at 30 thousand dollars per hundred units, and that rate of increase is itself decreasing.
choices.rationale: R′(20) = 30 is only the marginal revenue; the marginal profit also subtracts the marginal cost C′(20) = 16.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Profit is increasing at 14 thousand dollars per hundred units, and that rate of increase is itself increasing.
choices.rationale: P″ = R″ − C″ = −1 − 0.2 = −1.2 is negative, so the marginal profit is falling; claiming that the rate of increase is itself increasing gets the sign of P″ wrong.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Profit is increasing at 46 thousand dollars per hundred units, and that rate of increase is itself decreasing.
choices.rationale: 46 = 30 + 16 adds marginal revenue and marginal cost; profit is revenue minus cost, so the marginal cost must be subtracted.

title: combine marginal revenue and marginal cost into a marginal profit and read the sign of the second derivative as the tren (variant 2)
stem: A shop sells x units of an item at a constant price of $14 each, so its revenue is R(x) = 14x dollars. Its cost is C(x) = 100 + 6x + 40√x dollars. Which statement is correct at x = 25?

stem: The concentration of a drug in the blood, in mg/L, is C(t) = 8t/(t + 3), where t is the number of hours after the dose. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: At t = 3 the concentration is rising at 4 mg/L per hour, which is faster than its average rate of 8/9 mg/L per hour over [0, 6].
choices.rationale: The quotient rule gives C′(t) = 24/(t + 3)²; 24/(t + 3) = 4 leaves out squaring the denominator.

choices.label: B
choices.text: At t = 3 the concentration is rising at 2/3 mg/L per hour, which is slower than its average rate of 8/9 mg/L per hour over [0, 6].

choices.label: C
choices.text: At t = 3 the concentration is rising at 4/3 mg/L per hour, which is faster than its average rate of 8/9 mg/L per hour over [0, 6].
choices.rationale: 8/(t + 3) = 4/3 differentiates only the numerator and divides by the denominator; the quotient rule also needs the term from differentiating the denominator.

choices.label: D
choices.text: At t = 3 the concentration is falling at 2/3 mg/L per hour, while its average rate over [0, 6] is 8/9 mg/L per hour.
choices.rationale: The quotient rule numerator is 8(t + 3) − 8t = 24, which is positive, so C′(3) is positive and the concentration is rising, not falling.

title: differentiate a rational or exponential model, with units, and compare the instantaneous rate to an average rate over an (variant 1)
stem: The number of bacteria, in thousands, in a culture is P(t) = 60t/(t + 4), where t is the number of hours after the culture is started. Which statement is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: At t = 1 the population is growing at 9.6 thousand per hour, which is faster than its average rate of 5 thousand per hour over [0, 8].

choices.label: B
choices.text: At t = 1 the population is growing at 48 thousand per hour, which is faster than its average rate of 5 thousand per hour over [0, 8].
choices.rationale: The quotient rule gives P′(t) = 240/(t + 4)²; 240/(t + 4) = 48 leaves out squaring the denominator.

choices.label: C
choices.text: At t = 1 the population is growing at 12 thousand per hour, which is faster than its average rate of 5 thousand per hour over [0, 8].
choices.rationale: 60/(t + 4) = 12 differentiates only the numerator and divides by the denominator; the quotient rule also needs the term from differentiating the denominator.

choices.label: D
choices.text: At t = 1 the population is shrinking at 9.6 thousand per hour, while its average rate over [0, 8] is 5 thousand per hour.
choices.rationale: The quotient rule numerator is 60(t + 4) − 60t = 240, which is positive, so P′(1) is positive and the population is growing, not shrinking.

title: differentiate a rational or exponential model, with units, and compare the instantaneous rate to an average rate over an (variant 2)
stem: The amount of salt dissolved from a crystal after t minutes is Q(t) = 5(1 − e^(−0.4t)) grams. Which statement is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: At t = 3 the salt is dissolving at about 1.51 grams per minute, which is faster than its average rate of about 0.86 grams per minute over [0, 5].
choices.rationale: This omits the chain-rule factor 0.4 from differentiating the exponent: Q′(t) = 5·0.4e^(−0.4t) = 2e^(−0.4t), not 5e^(−0.4t).

choices.label: B
choices.text: At t = 3 the salt is dissolving at about 0.60 grams per minute, which is slower than its average rate of about 0.86 grams per minute over [0, 5].

choices.label: C
choices.text: At t = 3 the salt is dissolving at about −0.60 grams per minute, which is slower than its average rate of about 0.86 grams per minute over [0, 5].
choices.rationale: The derivative of −e^(−0.4t) is +0.4e^(−0.4t); keeping the minus sign makes the rate negative, but the amount dissolved is increasing.

choices.label: D
choices.text: At t = 3 the salt is dissolving at about 0.12 grams per minute, which is slower than its average rate of about 0.86 grams per minute over [0, 5].
choices.rationale: This drops the constant 5 and gets 0.4e^(−1.2); the factor 5 multiplies the whole derivative, giving 5·0.4e^(−1.2) = 2e^(−1.2).

title: differentiate a rational or exponential model, with units, and compare the instantaneous rate to an average rate over an (variant 3)
stem: The height of a plant, in centimeters, is H(t) = 12 ln(t + 1), where t is the number of days after planting. Which statement is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: At t = 5 the plant is growing at about 4.30 cm per day, which is faster than its average rate of about 3.30 cm per day over [0, 8].
choices.rationale: 12 ln 6/5 ≈ 4.30 is the average rate over [0, 5], not the instantaneous rate; the derivative H′(t) = 12/(t + 1) must be evaluated at t = 5.

choices.label: B
choices.text: At t = 5 the plant is growing at 2.4 cm per day, which is slower than its average rate of about 3.30 cm per day over [0, 8].
choices.rationale: 12/t = 2.4 differentiates ln(t + 1) as 1/t, forgetting the +1 inside the log; the derivative of ln(t + 1) is 1/(t + 1).

choices.label: C
choices.text: At t = 5 the plant is growing at 2 cm per day, which is slower than its average rate of about 3.30 cm per day over [0, 8].
choices.rationale: Correct: H′(t) = 12/(t + 1), so H′(5) = 2. The average rate is (H(8) − H(0))/8 = 12 ln 9/8 ≈ 3.296, and 2 < 3.296.

choices.label: D
choices.text: At t = 5 the plant is growing at about 0.33 cm per day, which is slower than its average rate of about 3.30 cm per day over [0, 8].
choices.rationale: 12/(t + 1)² = 1/3 uses a squared denominator, which belongs to the quotient rule; the derivative of ln(t + 1) is simply 1/(t + 1).

title: relate a changing hypotenuse to a changing leg by differentiating the Pythagorean relationship before substituting value
stem: A drone flies horizontally at a constant altitude of 60 m. An observer stands on the ground, and the drone moves away at 10 m/s. At the instant when its horizontal distance from the observer is 80 m, how fast is the straight-line distance from the observer to the drone increasing?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 10 m/s
choices.rationale: This treats the straight-line distance as changing at the same rate as the horizontal distance, but D′ = (x/D)x′ is smaller because the hypotenuse D = 100 is longer than x = 80.

choices.label: B
choices.text: 8 m/s
choices.rationale: Correct: D² = x² + 60², so 2D·D′ = 2x·x′ and D′ = (x/D)x′. At x = 80, D = 100, so D′ = (80/100)(10) = 8 m/s.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: This inverts the ratio: D′ = (x/D)(x′) uses x/D = 0.8, not D/x = 1.25, and the hypotenuse cannot grow faster than the leg that drives it here.

choices.label: D
choices.text: 6 m/s
choices.rationale: This multiplies by the altitude ratio 60/100 instead of the horizontal ratio 80/100; the altitude is constant and its rate is zero, so x is the factor that appears.

title: relate a changing hypotenuse to a changing leg by differentiating the Pythagorean relationship before substituting value (variant 1)
stem: A boat is pulled toward a dock by a rope attached to its bow and passing through a ring on the dock that is 6 ft above the bow. The rope is pulled in at 2 ft/s. When 10 ft of rope is out, how fast is the boat approaching the dock?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 2 ft/s
choices.rationale: This assumes the boat moves at the same rate as the rope, but the rope is the hypotenuse and the boat's horizontal distance changes at (L/x)(L′), which is faster.

choices.label: B
choices.text: 1.6 ft/s
choices.rationale: This inverts the ratio: x′ = (L/x)L′ uses L/x = 10/8, and the factor 8/10 puts the larger length in the wrong place, giving a slower rate.

choices.label: C
choices.text: 1.2 ft/s
choices.rationale: This multiplies by the ring height ratio 6/10 instead of L/x; the height is constant, so only the horizontal distance x enters the relationship.

choices.label: D
choices.text: 2.5 ft/s
choices.rationale: Correct: x² + 6² = L², so 2x·x′ = 2L·L′ and x′ = (L/x)L′. At L = 10, x = 8, so x′ = (10/8)(−2) = −2.5; the boat approaches at 2.5 ft/s.

title: relate a changing hypotenuse to a changing leg by differentiating the Pythagorean relationship before substituting value (variant 2)
stem: At a certain moment car P is 3 miles east of an intersection and moving toward it at 30 mph, while car Q is 4 miles north of the intersection and moving away from it at 40 mph. At that moment, how fast is the distance between the cars changing?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increasing at 14 mph
choices.rationale: Correct: D² = x² + y², so D′ = (x·x′ + y·y′)/D. With x = 3, x′ = −30, y = 4, y′ = 40 and D = 5, D′ = (−90 + 160)/5 = 14 mph.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increasing at 10 mph
choices.rationale: This adds the signed speeds, −30 + 40, as if the distance between the cars were a straight line along one road, ignoring that the distance is a hypotenuse.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increasing at 70 mph
choices.rationale: This computes x·x′ + y·y′ = 70 but forgets to divide by the distance D = 5; the relationship is D′ = (x·x′ + y·y′)/D.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Not changing, at 0 mph
choices.rationale: This pairs each speed with the other car's distance, 4(−30) + 3(40) = 0; x′ must be multiplied by x and y′ by y.

title: relate a changing hypotenuse to a changing leg by differentiating the Pythagorean relationship before substituting value (variant 3)
stem: The legs of a right triangular metal plate are x cm and y cm. As the plate is heated, x increases at 3 cm/min and y decreases at 2 cm/min. When x = 6 and y = 8, how fast is the hypotenuse changing?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increasing at 1 cm/min
choices.rationale: This adds the leg rates, 3 − 2 = 1, as if the hypotenuse were the sum of the legs; the hypotenuse satisfies z² = x² + y² and does not add linearly.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increasing at 2 cm/min
choices.rationale: This computes x·x′ + y·y′ = 18 − 16 = 2 but does not divide by the hypotenuse z = 10; the rate is (x·x′ + y·y′)/z.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increasing at 3.4 cm/min
choices.rationale: This treats the decreasing leg as increasing, using 18 + 16 = 34 divided by 10; the rate of y is −2, so its term is 8(−2) = −16.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increasing at 0.2 cm/min

title: set up the volume relationship for a cone or trough using the stated shape constraint, so that only one variable changes
stem: Sand falls from a conveyor at 10 ft³/min and forms a conical pile whose height always equals its base diameter. How fast is the height of the pile increasing when the height is 4 ft?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 15/(2π) ft/min
choices.rationale: This treats the radius as a constant 2 ft when differentiating V = (1/3)πr²h, so only the height changes; the radius r = h/2 grows with the height and must be replaced first.

choices.label: B
choices.text: 5/(2π) ft/min
choices.rationale: Correct: With r = h/2, V = (1/3)π(h/2)²h = πh³/12, so dV/dt = (π/4)h²·dh/dt. At h = 4, 10 = 4π·dh/dt, so dh/dt = 5/(2π) ft/min.

choices.label: C
choices.text: 5/(8π) ft/min
choices.rationale: This uses r = h, taking the height to equal the radius, but the height equals the base diameter, so r = h/2 and V = πh³/12.

choices.label: D
choices.text: 5/(32π) ft/min
choices.rationale: This inverts the relationship and uses r = 2h; the height equals the diameter 2r, so the radius is half the height, r = h/2.

title: set up the volume relationship for a cone or trough using the stated shape constraint, so that only one variable changes (variant 1)
stem: Gravel falls from a hopper at 6 ft³/min and forms a conical pile whose height is always 3 times its base radius. How fast is the height of the pile increasing when the height is 3 ft?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 18/π ft/min
choices.rationale: This treats the radius as a constant 1 ft when differentiating V = (1/3)πr²h; the radius r = h/3 grows with the height and must be replaced before differentiating.

choices.label: B
choices.text: 2/(3π) ft/min
choices.rationale: This uses r = h, taking the radius to equal the height, but the height is 3 times the radius, so r = h/3 and V = πh³/27.

choices.label: C
choices.text: 6/π ft/min
choices.rationale: Correct: With r = h/3, V = (1/3)π(h/3)²h = πh³/27, so dV/dt = (π/9)h²·dh/dt. At h = 3, 6 = π·dh/dt, so dh/dt = 6/π ft/min.

choices.label: D
choices.text: 2/(27π) ft/min
choices.rationale: This inverts the relationship and uses r = 3h; the height is three times the radius, so r = h/3 and not 3h.

title: set up the volume relationship for a cone or trough using the stated shape constraint, so that only one variable changes (variant 2)
stem: A horizontal trough is 10 ft long and its ends are triangles. The width of the water surface is always 1.5 times the depth h of the water. Water is poured in at 6 ft³/min. How fast is the depth increasing when the depth is 2 ft?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 0.1 ft/min
choices.rationale: This leaves out the factor 1/2 in the triangle's area, using V = 10(1.5h)(h) = 15h² instead of V = 10·(1/2)(1.5h)(h) = 7.5h².

choices.label: B
choices.text: 0.2 ft/min
choices.rationale: Correct: The end area is (1/2)(1.5h)(h) = 0.75h², so V = 7.5h² and dV/dt = 15h·dh/dt. At h = 2, 6 = 30·dh/dt, so dh/dt = 0.2 ft/min.

choices.label: C
choices.text: 0.4 ft/min
choices.rationale: This treats the surface width as a constant 3 ft when differentiating; the width 1.5h grows with the depth and must be replaced by 1.5h before differentiating.

choices.label: D
choices.text: 0.45 ft/min
choices.rationale: This inverts the ratio and uses width = h/1.5; the width is 1.5 times the depth, so the cross-sectional area is (1/2)(1.5h)(h) = 0.75h².

title: set up the volume relationship for a cone or trough using the stated shape constraint, so that only one variable changes (variant 3)
stem: Salt falls onto a table at 24 cm³/min and forms a conical pile whose base radius is always twice its height. How fast is the height of the pile increasing when the height is 3 cm?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 2/(3π) cm/min
choices.rationale: Correct: With r = 2h, V = (1/3)π(2h)²h = 4πh³/3, so dV/dt = 4πh²·dh/dt. At h = 3, 24 = 36π·dh/dt, so dh/dt = 2/(3π) cm/min.

choices.label: B
choices.text: 2/π cm/min
choices.rationale: This treats the radius as a constant 6 cm when differentiating V = (1/3)πr²h; the radius r = 2h grows with the height and must be replaced before differentiating.

choices.label: C
choices.text: 8/(3π) cm/min
choices.rationale: This uses r = h, taking the radius to equal the height, but the radius is twice the height, so V = (1/3)π(2h)²h = 4πh³/3.

choices.label: D
choices.text: 32/(3π) cm/min
choices.rationale: This inverts the relationship and uses r = h/2; the radius is twice the height, so r = 2h and not h/2.

title: solve a related-rates problem involving an angle or similar triangles by differentiating the trigonometric or proportion
stem: A camera on the ground is 90 m horizontally from the point where a drone lifts straight up at 15 m/s. When the drone is 120 m above the ground, how fast is the camera's angle of elevation to the drone changing?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 1/6 radian per second
choices.rationale: This differentiates tan θ = h/90 but treats dθ/dt as h′/90, dropping the factor sec²θ that comes from the chain rule on tan θ.

choices.label: B
choices.text: 25/54 radian per second
choices.rationale: This multiplies (1/6) by sec²θ = 25/9, but the equation sec²θ·θ′ = h′/90 requires dividing by sec²θ, which is the same as multiplying by cos²θ.

choices.label: C
choices.text: 3/32 radian per second
choices.rationale: This takes cos²θ as (90/120)², mixing up the hypotenuse with the height; at h = 120 the hypotenuse is 150 and cos θ = 90/150.

choices.label: D
choices.text: 0.06 radian per second
choices.rationale: Correct: tan θ = h/90, so sec²θ·θ′ = h′/90. At h = 120 the hypotenuse is 150, cos θ = 3/5 and sec²θ = 25/9, so θ′ = (15/90)(9/25) = 0.06 radian per second.

title: solve a related-rates problem involving an angle or similar triangles by differentiating the trigonometric or proportion (variant 1)
stem: A person 1.8 m tall walks directly away from a lamp post 6 m tall at 1.2 m/s. How fast is the tip of the person's shadow moving along the ground?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: This assumes the tip of the shadow moves at the same speed as the person, but similar triangles show the tip must move faster to stay ahead of the person.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: Correct: Let x be the person's distance from the lamp and T the tip's distance. Similar triangles give T/6 = (T − x)/1.8, so T = (10/7)x and T′ = (10/7)(1.2) = 12/7 m/s.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: This is the rate at which the shadow's length is growing, not the speed of its tip; the tip also moves with the person, so its speed is the sum.

choices.label: D
choices.text: 4 m/s
choices.rationale: This uses the ratio 6/1.8 from the heights directly; the similar triangles give 6/(6 − 1.8) = 10/7, not 6/1.8, as the factor multiplying the walking speed.

title: solve a related-rates problem involving an angle or similar triangles by differentiating the trigonometric or proportion (variant 2)
stem: A lighthouse is 3 km from a straight shore. Its beam rotates at 0.2 radian per minute and sweeps a spot along the shore. When the spot is 4 km from the point on shore nearest the lighthouse, how fast is the spot moving along the shore?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 5/3 km/min
choices.rationale: Correct: x = 3 tan θ, so x′ = 3 sec²θ·θ′. At x = 4 the beam length is 5, so sec θ = 5/3 and x′ = 3(25/9)(0.2) = 5/3 km/min.

choices.label: B
choices.text: 0.6 km/min
choices.rationale: This uses x′ = 3θ′ and leaves out the factor sec²θ that comes from differentiating x = 3 tan θ.

choices.label: C
choices.text: 16/15 km/min
choices.rationale: This takes sec²θ as (4/3)², mixing the shore distance 4 with the secant; at x = 4 the beam length is 5, so sec θ = 5/3 and sec²θ = 25/9.

choices.label: D
choices.text: 0.216 km/min
choices.rationale: This multiplies by cos²θ = 9/25 instead of sec²θ = 25/9; differentiating x = 3 tan θ gives x′ = 3 sec²θ·θ′.

title: solve a related-rates problem involving an angle or similar triangles by differentiating the trigonometric or proportion (variant 3)
stem: Two sides of a triangular sail are 8 m and 10 m long, and the angle θ between them increases at 0.1 radian per second. How fast is the area of the sail changing when θ = π/6?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 2 m²/s
choices.rationale: This uses sin(π/6) = 1/2 where the derivative of the area A = 40 sin θ, namely 40 cos θ·θ′, needs cos(π/6) = √3/2.

choices.label: B
choices.text: 2√3 m²/s

choices.label: C
choices.text: 4 m²/s
choices.rationale: This multiplies 40 by θ′ and drops the trigonometric factor entirely; the derivative of sin θ is cos θ, which must be evaluated at π/6.

choices.label: D
choices.text: 4√3 m²/s
choices.rationale: This uses A = 80 sin θ and omits the factor 1/2 in the triangle area formula A = (1/2)(8)(10) sin θ = 40 sin θ.

title: apply the product rule to a quantity that depends on two changing variables, keeping the sign of each rate.
stem: The radius of a cylindrical can increases at 0.2 cm/s while its height decreases at 0.5 cm/s. At the instant when r = 4 cm and h = 10 cm, which statement about the volume V = πr²h is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The volume is increasing at 16π cm³/s.
choices.rationale: This accounts for the growing radius, 2πrh·r′ = 16π, but leaves out the term πr²·h′ from the shrinking height.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The volume is increasing at 24π cm³/s.
choices.rationale: This treats the height's rate as +0.5 when computing πr²h′, adding 8π instead of subtracting it; the height is decreasing, so h′ = −0.5.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The volume is decreasing at 0.8π cm³/s.
choices.rationale: This multiplies the derivatives of the factors, π(2rr′)(h′), instead of using the product rule, which gives 2πrh·r′ + πr²·h′.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The volume is increasing at 8π cm³/s.
choices.rationale: Correct: V′ = π(2rh·r′ + r²·h′) = π(2·4·10·0.2 + 16·(−0.5)) = π(16 − 8) = 8π cm³/s, so the volume is increasing.

title: apply the product rule to a quantity that depends on two changing variables, keeping the sign of each rate. (variant 1)
stem: The length of a rectangular plate increases at 0.3 cm/s while its width decreases at 0.4 cm/s. At the instant when the length is 12 cm and the width is 8 cm, which statement about the area is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The area is increasing at 7.2 cm²/s.
choices.rationale: This treats the width's rate as +0.4, adding 12(0.4) = 4.8 to 0.3(8) = 2.4; the width is decreasing, so w′ = −0.4 and that term is −4.8.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The area is decreasing at 0.12 cm²/s.
choices.rationale: This multiplies the two rates, ℓ′·w′ = (0.3)(−0.4), instead of using the product rule A′ = ℓ′w + ℓw′.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The area is decreasing at 2.4 cm²/s.
choices.rationale: Correct: A = ℓw, so A′ = ℓ′w + ℓw′ = (0.3)(8) + (12)(−0.4) = 2.4 − 4.8 = −2.4 cm²/s, so the area is decreasing.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The area is increasing at 0.4 cm²/s.
choices.rationale: This computes ℓ·ℓ′ + w·w′ = 3.6 − 3.2, pairing each rate with its own dimension; the product rule pairs ℓ′ with w and w′ with ℓ.

title: apply the product rule to a quantity that depends on two changing variables, keeping the sign of each rate. (variant 2)
stem: A sealed syringe holds a gas whose pressure P and volume V satisfy PV = k at constant temperature. At the instant when P = 200 kPa and V = 1.5 L, the pressure is increasing at 10 kPa/min. Which statement is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The volume is increasing at 0.075 L/min.
choices.rationale: Differentiating PV = k gives P′V + PV′ = 0, so V′ = −VP′/P is negative; rising pressure at constant temperature means shrinking volume.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The volume is decreasing at 0.05 L/min.
choices.rationale: This uses V′ = −P′/P and drops the factor V = 1.5; solving P′V + PV′ = 0 gives V′ = −VP′/P = −1.5(10)/200.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The volume is decreasing at 0.075 L/min.
choices.rationale: Correct: PV = k gives P′V + PV′ = 0, so V′ = −V·P′/P = −(1.5)(10)/200 = −0.075 L/min.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The volume is decreasing at about 1333 L/min.
choices.rationale: This inverts the ratio, V′ = −(P/V)P′, but solving P′V + PV′ = 0 for V′ gives −(V/P)P′, with V on top.

title: apply the product rule to a quantity that depends on two changing variables, keeping the sign of each rate. (variant 3)
stem: The radius of a cone increases at 0.5 cm/s while its height decreases at 1 cm/s. At the instant when r = 6 cm and h = 9 cm, which statement about the volume V = (1/3)πr²h is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The volume is increasing at 18π cm³/s.
choices.rationale: This applies the product rule correctly but leaves out the factor 1/3 from V = (1/3)πr²h, tripling the result.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The volume is increasing at 30π cm³/s.
choices.rationale: This treats the height's rate as +1 and adds r² to 2rh·r′ inside the parentheses; the height is decreasing, so h′ = −1.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The volume is decreasing at 2π cm³/s.
choices.rationale: This multiplies the derivatives of the factors, (π/3)(2rr′)(h′), instead of using the product rule, which gives (π/3)(2rh·r′ + r²·h′).

choices.label: D
choices.text: The volume is increasing at 6π cm³/s.
choices.rationale: Correct: V′ = (π/3)(2rh·r′ + r²·h′) = (π/3)(2·6·9·0.5 + 36·(−1)) = (π/3)(54 − 36) = 6π cm³/s, so the volume is increasing.

title: use a tangent-line approximation at the correct point and decide whether it overestimates or underestimates from the con
stem:
A differentiable function f has f(3) = 4, and f′ is decreasing on the interval [2, 4]. Selected values of f′ are given.
x | f′(x)
2.5 | 1.5
3 | 1.1
3.5 | 0.6
4 | 0.2
The tangent line at x = 3 is used to approximate f(3.4). Which statement is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The approximation is 4.44, and it is an underestimate of f(3.4).
choices.rationale: F′ is decreasing, so f″ < 0 and f is concave down; a tangent line to a concave-down graph lies above the graph, so it overestimates.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The approximation is 4.24, and it is an overestimate of f(3.4).
choices.rationale: This uses the slope f′(3.5) = 0.6, the table value nearest 3.4, but the tangent line at x = 3 must use the slope at the point of tangency, f′(3) = 1.1.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The approximation is 4.44, and it is an overestimate of f(3.4).
choices.rationale: Correct: L(x) = f(3) + f′(3)(x − 3) = 4 + 1.1(0.4) = 4.44. Since f′ is decreasing, f″ < 0, the graph is concave down and lies below its tangent line, so 4.44 overestimates f(3.4).

choices.label: D
choices.text: The approximation is 3.56, and it is an underestimate of f(3.4).
choices.rationale: This subtracts f′(3)(0.4) even though 3.4 is to the right of 3; the tangent line gives f(3) + f′(3)(3.4 − 3) = 4 + 0.44.

title: use a tangent-line approximation at the correct point and decide whether it overestimates or underestimates from the con (variant 1)
stem: Let h(x) = e^(x/2). The tangent line at x = 0 is used to approximate h(0.6). Which statement is correct?
